rationale:
This is decomposition attempt 3 for this node. Attempts 1 and 2 (nodes/root-flat-iff-weak-a1-tangent-locality-a1/decomposition-v1.json and -v2.json) proposed this same four-child split. Both independent audits (decomposition-audit-v1/v2.json) accepted it, after replaying Lean proofs of all four children and of the exact parent assembly with only standard axioms. Neither attempt was published. The issue worker that wrote them (issue-workers.json, started 2026-10-12T02:22:58Z) never completed, and the controller restarted (run.json created 11:21:39Z; the node is now at attempt 3). No invalidity reason was recorded (Correction: None). This attempt therefore re-proposes the split with byte-identical lean_names, frozen lean_statements and dependencies, after the independent re-validation below. The natural proofs are v2's verbatim except for one added sentence in ae_l1_density step 6(i), which states the side conditions of ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt.

Why split. The supplied proof contains four distinct, reusable obligations.
1. fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral (parent step 1): the change of variables ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} g dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_S g∘η_{x,r} dHⁿ, for arbitrary S and g. It is used by both growth_bound and transfer. SimonGMT's analogue (Chapter04 WeightedBlowUp) lies outside the frozen import closure. The alpha-equivalent lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image belongs to another branch and has status rlcr-lean, so it is not accepted and cannot be reused.
2. fiw_tl_growth_bound (parent step 4(i)): at a weighted approximate tangent point, ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ⁺ ≤ (C sⁿ)⁺ for small s.
3. fiw_tl_transfer (parent steps 1 and 4(iii)–(iv)): a deterministic pointwise lemma. Relative L¹-closeness of 1_{M₂}θ₂ to c·1_{M₁}θ₁ on small balls, together with θ₂(x) = cθ₁(x), carries the tangent space from (M₁,θ₁) to (M₂,θ₂). The parent's three error terms (J₂, the (g − g(x))θ₁ term and the M₁∖A term) are bundled into one L¹ quantity.
4. fiw_tl_ae_l1_density (parent steps 2, 3 and 4(ii)): the almost-everywhere analytic core. It uses Besicovitch density of A = M₁ ∩ M₂ for ν₂ = θ₂Hⁿ⌞M₂ and Lebesgue points of g = 1_A θ₂/θ₁ for ν₁, after localizing to compact balls. Positivity of θ_i turns ν_i-null sets into Hⁿ-null sets.
This isolates Besicovitch/Vitali differentiation from the blow-up calculus.

How the children imply the parent (exact assembly, checked in Lean).
- Let A = M₁ ∩ M₂. fiw_tl_ae_l1_density has exactly the parent's hypotheses. For (μHE[n]⌞A)-a.e. x it gives: for every ε > 0 and all s near 0⁺, ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖1_{M₂}θ₂ − (θ₂x/θ₁x)·1_{M₁}θ₁‖ₑ ≤ ofReal ε·∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal θ₁.
- Intersect with x ∈ A (ae_restrict_mem₀; A is null-measurable). Fix such an x and any Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x Q.
- U is open and x ∈ M₁ ⊆ U, so choose δ > 0 with ball x δ ⊆ U and set ρ = δ/2. Then closedBall x ρ is a compact subset of U, so θ_i is integrable on M_i ∩ closedBall x ρ.
- θ₁ ≥ 0 on M₁, and θ₂ x = (θ₂ x/θ₁ x)·θ₁ x because θ₁ x > 0.
- fiw_tl_transfer with c = θ₂x/θ₁x then gives HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x Q.
- The exceptional null set comes only from fiw_tl_ae_l1_density and does not depend on Q. This is exactly the frozen type ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (M₁ ∩ M₂)), ∀ Q, ….

subproblems.title: Blow-up change of variables for μHE[n] under η_{x,r}
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P = Eucl P, x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0, S ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set and g : ℝ^P → ℝ an arbitrary function. Let η := η_{x,r} = blowUpMap x r, so η(z) = r⁻¹(z − x). Then the Bochner integrals satisfy ∫_{η(S)} g dH = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · ∫_S g(η(z)) dH(z). No measurability or integrability assumption is made; a non-integrable integrand has integral 0 on either side.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (x : Eucl P) (r : ℝ) (S : Set (Eucl P)) (g : Eucl P → ℝ), 0 < r → ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' S, g y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) = (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in S, g (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and 1.8(1)), where η_{x,r} = blowUpMap x r and Hⁿ = μHE[n] is translation invariant and n-homogeneous. Notation: H := μHE[n] and η := blowUpMap x r, η(z) = r⁻¹ • (z − x), with r > 0.

1. η is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P. It is continuous, and w ↦ x + r • w is a continuous two-sided inverse: r⁻¹ • ((x + r•w) − x) = w and x + r • (r⁻¹ • (z − x)) = z, using r ≠ 0. Hence η is a bijection and a measurable embedding (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding).

2. Scaling of preimages. For every set F ⊆ ℝ^P, η⁻¹(F) = τ_x(r • F), where τ_x(w) = x + w (IsometryEquiv.addLeft x) and r • F = {r•w : w ∈ F}. Indeed z ∈ η⁻¹(F) iff w := r⁻¹ • (z − x) ∈ F, and then z = x + r • w. Translation is an isometry, so H(τ_x(E)) = H(E) for every set E (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Also H(r • F) = ‖r‖₊ⁿ · H(F) = rⁿ · H(F) for every set F (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, r ≠ 0). Therefore H(η⁻¹(F)) = rⁿ · H(F) for every F ⊆ ℝ^P.

3. Push-forward identity: map η (H⌞S) = rⁿ · H⌞η(S). Let E be measurable. Then η⁻¹(E) is measurable, and (map η (H⌞S))(E) = (H⌞S)(η⁻¹(E)) = H(η⁻¹(E) ∩ S) by Measure.map_apply and Measure.restrict_apply. Since η is a bijection, η⁻¹(E) ∩ S = η⁻¹(E ∩ η(S)). By step 2 this is rⁿ · H(E ∩ η(S)) = rⁿ · (H⌞η(S))(E). Measures agreeing on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext).

4. Change of variables along a measurable embedding needs no integrability (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). It gives ∫_S g(η(z)) dH(z) = ∫ (g ∘ η) d(H⌞S) = ∫ g d(map η (H⌞S)).

5. By step 3 and integral_smul_measure (∫ g d(c·μ) = c.toReal · ∫ g dμ for every g and c ∈ [0,∞]): ∫ g d(map η (H⌞S)) = rⁿ · ∫ g d(H⌞η(S)) = rⁿ · ∫_{η(S)} g dH. Here the scalar (‖r‖₊ⁿ : ℝ≥0∞) has toReal equal to rⁿ.

6. Steps 4 and 5 give rⁿ · ∫_{η(S)} g dH = ∫_S g(η(z)) dH(z). Since rⁿ > 0, multiplying by (rⁿ)⁻¹ yields ∫_{η(S)} g dH = (rⁿ)⁻¹ · ∫_S g(η(z)) dH(z). ∎
proof_key_steps: η = blowUpMap x r is a homeomorphism with inverse w ↦ x + r•w, hence a bijective measurable embedding.
For every set F, η⁻¹(F) = x + r•F, so H(η⁻¹F) = rⁿH(F) by isometry invariance and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
map η (H⌞S) = rⁿ • H⌞η(S), checked on measurable E via η⁻¹(E) ∩ S = η⁻¹(E ∩ η(S)).
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure give rⁿ∫_{η(S)} g dH = ∫_S g∘η dH; divide by rⁿ > 0.

subproblems.title: Upper n-density bound at a weighted approximate tangent point
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be H-null-measurable and θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ ≥ 0 on M. Let x ∈ ℝ^P and ρ > 0 with θ H-integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x). Let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q (Simon Ch. 3, 1.7). Then there is C ∈ ℝ such that for all sufficiently small s > 0 (∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] 0): ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ(z)) dH(z) ≤ ofReal(C·sⁿ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (x : Eucl P) (ρ : ℝ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P)), 0 < ρ → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ y ∈ M, 0 ≤ θ y) → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ closedBall x ρ) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ∫⁻ z in M ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * s ^ n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(i) of the parent-supplied proof (growth of ν₁ from the tangent hypothesis), stated for a single pair (M, θ). Notation: H := μHE[n], η_s := blowUpMap x s, and t⁺ := ENNReal.ofReal t. Note ‖η_s(z)‖ = ‖z − x‖/s for s > 0.

1. Test function. Let φ(y) := max(0, min(1, 2 − ‖y‖)). Then φ is continuous and 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1. Also φ(y) = 1 if ‖y‖ ≤ 1 and φ(y) = 0 if ‖y‖ ≥ 2. So φ vanishes outside the compact ball B̄_2(0) and defines f₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). In Lean write CompactlySupportedContinuousMap (Eucl P) ℝ, since the C_c notation needs `open scoped CompactlySupported`, and build it with HasCompactSupport.intro (isCompact_closedBall 0 2).

2. Use of the hypothesis. Let I(s) := ∫_{η_s(M)} f₀(y)·θ(x + s•y) dH(y). The second component of HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt, applied to f₀, gives I(s) → L := θ(x)·∫_Q f₀ dH as s → 0⁺. Put C := |L| + 1 > L. Then there is s₁ > 0 with I(s) < C for all s ∈ (0, s₁) (Tendsto.eventually with gt_mem_nhds).

3. Fix s with 0 < s < min(s₁, ρ/2). Apply the sibling lemma fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral with S = M, r = s and g(y) = f₀(y)θ(x + s•y). Since x + s•η_s(z) = z, this gives I(s) = s^{−n}·∫_M F dH, where F(z) := f₀(η_s(z))·θ(z).

4. Properties of F:
(a) If ‖z − x‖ > ρ, then ‖η_s(z)‖ > ρ/s > 2, so F(z) = 0.
(b) If z ∈ B̄_s(x), then ‖η_s(z)‖ ≤ 1, so F(z) = θ(z).
(c) F ≥ 0 on M, because f₀ ≥ 0 and θ ≥ 0 on M.
(d) f₀∘η_s is continuous with |f₀∘η_s| ≤ 1.

5. Integrability of F on M. F is integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x): it is a bounded continuous factor times the integrable θ (Integrable.bdd_mul). By 4(a), F = 0 on M ∖ B̄_ρ(x). Since M is null-measurable, F is integrable on M (IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).

6. Comparison:
∫_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ dH = ∫_{M∩B̄_s(x)} F dH, by 4(b) and setIntegral_congr_fun₀ on the null-measurable set M ∩ B̄_s(x);
≤ ∫_M F dH, by setIntegral_mono_set (F is integrable on M, F ≥ 0 a.e. for H⌞M by 4(c) and ae_restrict_mem₀, and M ∩ B̄_s(x) ⊆ M);
= sⁿ·I(s), by step 3;
≤ C·sⁿ, by step 2 and sⁿ > 0.

7. θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_s(x) ⊆ M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) (IntegrableOn.mono_set), and θ ≥ 0 a.e. there. So ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ⁺ dH = (∫_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ dH)⁺ by ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal. This is ≤ (C·sⁿ)⁺ by step 6 and monotonicity of ENNReal.ofReal.

8. Steps 3–7 hold for every s ∈ (0, min(s₁, ρ/2)). Combining the eventual statement of step 2 with Ioo_mem_nhdsGT (half_pos hρ), the bound holds for all sufficiently small s > 0, with the constant C of step 2. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose f₀(y) = max(0, min(1, 2 − ‖y‖)) ∈ C_c, with 1_{B̄_1(0)} ≤ f₀ ≤ 1 and support in B̄_2(0).
The tangent hypothesis gives I(s) → θ(x)∫_Q f₀ dH, so I(s) < C := |L| + 1 for small s.
By the change of variables, I(s) = s^{−n}∫_M f₀(η_s z)θ(z) dH(z).
F = (f₀∘η_s)θ is integrable on M, nonnegative on M, and equals θ on B̄_s(x), so ∫_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ ≤ ∫_M F = sⁿI(s) ≤ C sⁿ.
Convert to a lintegral with ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal.

subproblems.title: Pointwise transfer of weighted approximate tangent spaces under relative L¹-closeness
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M₁ M₂ : Set (Eucl P)) (θ₁ θ₂ : Eucl P → ℝ) (x : Eucl P) (c ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → NullMeasurableSet M₁ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → NullMeasurableSet M₂ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ y ∈ M₁, 0 ≤ θ₁ y) → IntegrableOn θ₁ (M₁ ∩ closedBall x ρ) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → IntegrableOn θ₂ (M₂ ∩ closedBall x ρ) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → θ₂ x = c * θ₁ x → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ∫⁻ z in closedBall x s, ‖M₂.indicator θ₂ z - c * M₁.indicator θ₁ z‖ₑ ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε * ∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₁ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x Q → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4(iii)–(iv) of the parent-supplied proof. The three error terms there are bundled into the single function h := 1_{M₂}θ₂ − c·1_{M₁}θ₁, whose smallness is hypothesis (iv). Notation: H := μHE[n], η_r := blowUpMap x r, t⁺ := ENNReal.ofReal t, and I_i(r) := ∫_{η_r(M_i)} f(y)·θ_i(x + r•y) dH(y) for i = 1, 2.

1. Fix Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x Q. Its first component, finrank Q = n, is the first component of the goal. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). We must show I₂(r) → θ₂(x)·∫_Q f dH as r → 0⁺.

2. Growth. Apply the sibling lemma fiw_tl_growth_bound to M₁, θ₁, x, ρ, Q, using (i), (ii) and null-measurability of M₁. This gives C₀ ∈ ℝ with ∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} θ₁⁺ dH ≤ (C₀sⁿ)⁺ for all sufficiently small s > 0. Put C₁ := max(C₀, 0).

3. Bounds on f. There is R > 0 with f(y) = 0 whenever R ≤ ‖y‖ (HasCompactSupport.exists_pos_le_norm). There is K ≥ 0 with |f(y)| ≤ K for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). For r > 0, ‖η_r(z)‖ = ‖z − x‖/r, so f(η_r(z)) = 0 whenever R·r ≤ ‖z − x‖.

4. Representation. Let r > 0 and i ∈ {1, 2}. Apply fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral with S = M_i and g(y) = f(y)θ_i(x + r•y), and use x + r•η_r(z) = z. This gives I_i(r) = r^{−n}·∫_{M_i} f(η_r z)θ_i(z) dH(z). Since M_i is null-measurable (integral_indicator₀) and by indicator_mul_right, this equals r^{−n}·∫ G_i dH with G_i(z) := f(η_r(z))·(1_{M_i}θ_i)(z).

5. Integrability. Let 0 < r with R·r < ρ. If z ∉ B̄_ρ(x), then ‖z − x‖ > ρ > R·r, so f(η_r(z)) = 0. Hence G_i(z) = f(η_r(z))·(1_{M_i ∩ B̄_ρ(x)}θ_i)(z) for all z. The function 1_{M_i∩B̄_ρ(x)}θ_i is H-integrable by (ii) (IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator₀ on the null-measurable set). The factor f∘η_r is continuous and bounded by K. So G_i is H-integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul).

6. Key estimate. Put h := 1_{M₂}θ₂ − c·1_{M₁}θ₁. For 0 < r with R·r < ρ, steps 4–5 and linearity (integral_sub, integral_const_mul) give I₂(r) − c·I₁(r) = r^{−n}·∫ f(η_r(z))·h(z) dH(z). Hence, in [0, ∞]:
‖I₂(r) − c·I₁(r)‖ₑ ≤ (r^{−n})⁺·∫⁻ ‖f(η_r z)·h(z)‖ₑ dH(z), by enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm;
≤ (r^{−n})⁺·K⁺·∫⁻_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖h‖ₑ dH.
For the last inequality: on B̄_{Rr}(x) bound |f(η_r z)| ≤ K; off it f(η_r(z)) = 0 by step 3; then use lintegral_indicator for the closed ball and lintegral_const_mul'.

7. The difference tends to 0. Let ε > 0 and put ε' := ε / (2(K·C₁·Rⁿ + 1)) > 0. As r → 0⁺ we have s = R·r → 0⁺, since R > 0: r ↦ R·r maps 𝓝[>] 0 into 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). So for all sufficiently small r > 0, hypothesis (iv) with ε' and step 2 both hold at s = R·r; also R·r < ρ. For such r:
∫⁻_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖h‖ₑ dH ≤ ε'⁺·(C₀(Rr)ⁿ)⁺ ≤ (ε'·C₁·Rⁿ·rⁿ)⁺.
By step 6, |I₂(r) − c·I₁(r)| ≤ r^{−n}·K·ε'·C₁·Rⁿ·rⁿ = K·C₁·Rⁿ·ε' < ε, after converting with ofReal_norm and ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff. Thus I₂(r) − c·I₁(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺ (Metric.tendsto_nhds).

8. By the hypothesis on (M₁, θ₁), I₁(r) → θ₁(x)·∫_Q f dH. So c·I₁(r) → c·θ₁(x)·∫_Q f dH = θ₂(x)·∫_Q f dH, by (iii). Adding the limit of step 7, I₂(r) = (I₂(r) − c·I₁(r)) + c·I₁(r) → θ₂(x)·∫_Q f dH.

9. f was arbitrary and finrank Q = n, so HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: finrank Q = n is inherited; fix f ∈ C_c with f = 0 off B_R(0) and |f| ≤ K.
fiw_tl_growth_bound gives ∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} θ₁⁺ ≤ (C₀sⁿ)⁺ for small s.
fiw_tl_blowup_setIntegral and integral_indicator₀ give I_i(r) = r^{−n}∫ f(η_r z)(1_{M_i}θ_i)(z) dH, with integrable integrands once R r < ρ.
|I₂(r) − cI₁(r)| ≤ r^{−n}K∫⁻_{B̄_{Rr}(x)}|1_{M₂}θ₂ − c1_{M₁}θ₁| dH.
With s = Rr, the L¹-closeness hypothesis and the growth bound give |I₂ − cI₁| ≤ K C₁ Rⁿ ε' → 0.
cI₁(r) → cθ₁(x)∫_Q f = θ₂(x)∫_Q f, hence I₂(r) → θ₂(x)∫_Q f.

subproblems.title: A.e. relative L¹-density of 1_{M₂}θ₂ against (θ₂(x)/θ₁(x))·1_{M₁}θ₁ via Besicovitch and Lebesgue points
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and M₁, M₂ ⊆ U H-null-measurable. Let θ₁, θ₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ_i > 0 on M_i and θ_i H-integrable on M_i ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U (i = 1, 2). Then for H⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂)-almost every x the following holds: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently small s > 0, ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖1_{M₂}θ₂ − (θ₂(x)/θ₁(x))·1_{M₁}θ₁‖ₑ dH ≤ ofReal(ε)·∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ₁) dH.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (M₁ M₂ : Set (Eucl P)) (θ₁ θ₂ : Eucl P → ℝ), M₁ ⊆ U → M₂ ⊆ U → NullMeasurableSet M₁ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → NullMeasurableSet M₂ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ x ∈ M₁, 0 < θ₁ x) → (∀ x ∈ M₂, 0 < θ₂ x) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ₁ (M₁ ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ₂ (M₂ ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M₁ ∩ M₂)), ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ∫⁻ z in closedBall x s, ‖M₂.indicator θ₂ z - θ₂ x / θ₁ x * M₁.indicator θ₁ z‖ₑ ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε * ∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₁ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2, 3 and 4(ii)–(iii) of the parent-supplied proof (Besicovitch differentiation for the Radon measures θ_iHⁿ⌞M_i). The parent's error terms are collected into one L¹ quantity. Simplification: the ν₁-density of A (parent step 3(a) for i = 1) is not needed. Since g = 0 on M₁∖A and g(x) = c > 0, the Lebesgue-point integral ∫_B|g − c| dν₁ already contains c·ν₁(B∖A).

Notation: H := μHE[n], A := M₁ ∩ M₂ (H-null-measurable), B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s, B_r(y) = ball y r, t⁺ := ENNReal.ofReal t. Let Φ(x) denote the conclusion at x: for every ε > 0, for all small s > 0, ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖1_{M₂}θ₂ − (θ₂(x)/θ₁(x))·1_{M₁}θ₁‖ₑ dH ≤ ε⁺·∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} θ₁⁺ dH.

1. Reduction to balls. Let 𝓘 be the set of pairs (y, r) ∈ ℝ^P × ℝ with B̄_r(y) ⊆ U. Every x ∈ U lies in some B_r(y) with (y, r) ∈ 𝓘: choose δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ U and take (x, δ/2). ℝ^P is second countable, so there is a countable T ⊆ 𝓘 with ⋃_{(y,r)∈T} B_r(y) = ⋃_{(y,r)∈𝓘} B_r(y) ⊇ U (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). Since A ⊆ U, A = ⋃_{(y,r)∈T} (A ∩ B_r(y)). By ae_restrict_biUnion_iff (T countable) it suffices to prove: for each (y, r) with B̄_r(y) ⊆ U, Φ(x) holds for H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y))-a.e. x. Fix such (y, r) and put K := B̄_r(y), a compact subset of U. By hypothesis θ_i is H-integrable on M_i ∩ K.

2. Localized weighted measures. For i = 1, 2 let ν_i := (H⌞(M_i ∩ K)).withDensity(θ_i⁺). Then:
(a) ν_i(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_{M_i∩K} θ_i⁺ dH ≤ ∫⁻_{M_i∩K} |θ_i| dH < ∞, so ν_i is a finite Borel measure, hence locally finite and s-finite.
(b) ν_i ≪ H⌞(M_i∩K) ≪ H (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
(c) θ_i⁺ is a.e.-measurable for H⌞(M_i∩K) and nonzero H⌞(M_i∩K)-a.e., since θ_i > 0 on M_i (ae_restrict_mem₀). Hence H⌞(M_i ∩ K) ≪ ν_i (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous').
Consequently A is null-measurable for ν_i and for H⌞(M_i∩K), since both measures are ≪ H. Moreover (H⌞(M_i∩K))⌞A = H⌞(A ∩ M_i ∩ K) (Measure.restrict_restrict₀), and A ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ A ∩ M_i ∩ K because A ⊆ M_i and B_r(y) ⊆ K; hence H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y)) ≤ (H⌞(M_i∩K))⌞A (Measure.restrict_mono). Restricting (c) to A gives (H⌞(M_i∩K))⌞A ≪ ν_i⌞A (AbsolutelyContinuous.restrict). So H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y)) ≪ ν_i⌞A, and since ν_i⌞A ≤ ν_i also H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y)) ≪ ν_i.

3. The density g. Let g := 1_A·(θ₂/θ₁), i.e. g(z) = θ₂(z)/θ₁(z) on A and 0 elsewhere. θ₁ and θ₂ are a.e.-measurable for H⌞(A∩K), so g is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞(M₁∩K) (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀), hence for ν₁. For z ∈ M₁ ∩ K, θ₁(z)⁺·|g(z)| ≤ 1_{M₂∩K}(z)·θ₂(z)⁺: it equals θ₂(z)⁺ if z ∈ A and 0 otherwise. Using lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀:
∫⁻|g| dν₁ = ∫⁻ θ₁⁺|g| d(H⌞(M₁∩K)) ≤ ∫⁻_{M₂∩K} θ₂⁺ dH < ∞.
So g ∈ L¹(ν₁).

4. Differentiation theorems. ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional normed space, so it has the Besicovitch covering property (instHasBesicovitchCovering) and is second countable.
(a) Besicovitch density theorem for ν₂ and the arbitrary set A (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div ν₂ A): for ν₂⌞A-a.e. x, ν₂(A ∩ B̄_s(x))/ν₂(B̄_s(x)) → 1 as s → 0⁺.
(b) Lebesgue differentiation theorem: for ν₁-a.e. x, (∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖g − g(x)‖ₑ dν₁)/ν₁(B̄_s(x)) → 0 as s → 0⁺. Use VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν₁ and g, composed with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν₁ x.
By step 2 (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le), both hold for H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y))-a.e. x, as does x ∈ A ∩ B_r(y) (ae_restrict_mem₀). Fix such an x; it remains to prove Φ(x).

5. Constants at x. x ∈ A, so θ₁(x), θ₂(x) > 0. Put c := θ₂(x)/θ₁(x) > 0; then g(x) = c. Fix ε > 0 and put δ := min(1/2, ε/(3c + 3)) > 0, so δ ≤ 1/2 and δ(3c + 3) ≤ ε. For all sufficiently small s > 0 the following hold simultaneously:
(E0) B := B̄_s(x) ⊆ K: true whenever s < r − dist(x, y), as x ∈ B_r(y).
(E2) ν₂(A ∩ B)/ν₂(B) > (1 − δ)⁺, from 4(a), since (1 − δ)⁺ < 1 (lt_mem_nhds).
(E3) (∫⁻_B ‖g − c‖ₑ dν₁)/ν₁(B) < δ⁺, from 4(b) (gt_mem_nhds).
Fix such an s. We prove the inequality of Φ(x) at s.

6. Consequences. All ν_i(B) < ∞.
(i) ν₂(B ∖ A) ≤ δ⁺·ν₂(B). From (E2), (1 − δ)⁺·ν₂(B) < ν₂(A ∩ B) by ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt. Its side conditions ν₂(B) ≠ 0 ∨ (1 − δ)⁺ ≠ ∞ and ν₂(B) ≠ ∞ ∨ (1 − δ)⁺ ≠ 0 hold because ν₂(B) < ∞. Also ν₂(B) = ν₂(B ∩ A) + ν₂(B ∖ A) (measure_inter_add_sdiff₀; A is ν₂-null-measurable). Pass to real numbers.
(ii) I := ∫⁻_B ‖g − c‖ₑ dν₁ ≤ δ⁺·ν₁(B). This is trivial if I = 0. Otherwise (E3) and ENNReal.div_lt_iff give I < δ⁺·ν₁(B). That lemma reads c' / b < a ↔ c' < a * b with side conditions b ≠ 0 ∨ c' ≠ 0 and b ≠ ∞ ∨ c' ≠ ∞, where c' is the numerator.
(iii) Integral identities, using that B is measurable and B ⊆ K:
- ν₁(B) = ∫⁻_{M₁∩B} θ₁⁺ dH (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, B ∩ (M₁∩K) = M₁ ∩ B);
- I = ∫⁻_{M₁∩B} θ₁⁺·‖g − c‖ₑ dH (setLIntegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀);
- ν₂(B ∖ A) = ∫⁻_{(M₂∖M₁)∩B} θ₂⁺ dH;
- ν₂(A ∩ B) = ∫⁻_{A∩B} θ₂⁺ dH.
The last two use withDensity_apply₀ and Measure.restrict_restrict₀ on null-measurable sets, with (B∖A) ∩ (M₂∩K) = (M₂∖M₁) ∩ B and (A∩B) ∩ (M₂∩K) = A ∩ B.
(iv) ν₂(A ∩ B) ≤ c⁺·ν₁(B) + I. For z ∈ A, θ₂(z) = g(z)θ₁(z) ≤ cθ₁(z) + θ₁(z)|g(z) − c|, so θ₂(z)⁺ ≤ c⁺θ₁(z)⁺ + θ₁(z)⁺‖g(z) − c‖ₑ. Integrate over A ∩ B (lintegral_mono_ae), enlarge to M₁ ∩ B (lintegral_mono_set), split with lintegral_add_left' (first summand a.e.-measurable) and lintegral_const_mul', then use (iii).

7. Pointwise decomposition. For every z ∈ B,
‖1_{M₂}θ₂(z) − c·1_{M₁}θ₁(z)‖ₑ ≤ 1_{M₁∩B}(z)·θ₁(z)⁺‖g(z) − c‖ₑ + 1_{(M₂∖M₁)∩B}(z)·θ₂(z)⁺.
Check by cases:
- z ∈ A: the left side is |θ₂(z) − cθ₁(z)| = θ₁(z)·|θ₂(z)/θ₁(z) − c| = θ₁(z)|g(z) − c|.
- z ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂: g(z) = 0 and the left side is cθ₁(z) = θ₁(z)|0 − c|.
- z ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁: the left side is θ₂(z).
- Otherwise the left side is 0.
Integrate over B (setLIntegral_mono'). The second summand is a.e.-measurable for H⌞B (aemeasurable_indicator_iff₀; θ₂ is a.e.-measurable for H⌞((M₂∖M₁)∩B) ≤ H⌞(M₂∩K)), so lintegral_add_right' splits the integral. Enlarge H⌞B to H in both terms, use lintegral_indicator₀, and apply (iii):
∫⁻_B ‖1_{M₂}θ₂ − c·1_{M₁}θ₁‖ₑ dH ≤ I + ν₂(B ∖ A).

8. Final arithmetic. Write b₁ = ν₁(B), b₂ = ν₂(B), a₂ = ν₂(A ∩ B), d₂ = ν₂(B ∖ A), all finite.
- From (i), b₂ = a₂ + d₂ ≤ a₂ + δb₂, so (1 − δ)b₂ ≤ a₂.
- Since δ ≤ 1/2, b₂ ≤ 2a₂ ≤ 2(c·b₁ + I) ≤ 2(c + δ)b₁, by (iv) and (ii).
- Hence I + d₂ ≤ δb₁ + δb₂ ≤ δ(1 + 2c + 2δ)b₁ ≤ δ(3c + 3)b₁ ≤ ε·b₁.
With step 7 and b₁ = ∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} θ₁⁺ dH (step 6(iii)), this is exactly the inequality of Φ(x) at s. It holds for all sufficiently small s > 0 and every ε > 0, so Φ(x) holds. This proves the local statement of step 1, and hence the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover U by countably many balls B_r(y) with B̄_r(y) ⊆ U (isOpen_iUnion_countable); by ae_restrict_biUnion_iff it suffices to work on A ∩ B_r(y) with K = B̄_r(y).
ν_i := (H⌞(M_i∩K)).withDensity(θ_i⁺) are finite, and H⌞(M_i∩K) ≪ ν_i because θ_i > 0 on M_i, so ν_i-null sets inside A ∩ K are H-null.
g := 1_A θ₂/θ₁ ∈ L¹(ν₁).
Besicovitch density of A for ν₂ and the Lebesgue point of g for ν₁ hold at H⌞(A∩B_r(y))-a.e. x.
At such x, with c = θ₂(x)/θ₁(x) = g(x) and small s: ν₂(B∖A) ≤ δν₂(B), ∫_B|g − c|dν₁ ≤ δν₁(B), and ν₂(A∩B) ≤ cν₁(B) + ∫_B|g − c|dν₁.
Pointwise, |1_{M₂}θ₂ − c1_{M₁}θ₁| ≤ 1_{M₁}θ₁|g − c| + 1_{M₂∖M₁}θ₂ on B, so ∫_B|…| dH ≤ ∫_B|g − c|dν₁ + ν₂(B∖A) ≤ δ(3c+3)ν₁(B) ≤ εν₁(B).
